chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Hashim ibn Hanan, from Abu Sa'id al-Mukari, from Abu Basir, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man divorces his wife while he is absent, and he knows that on the day he divorced her, she was menstruating. He said: It is valid.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: These narrations have come generally regarding the validity of the absent person's divorce in all cases, but it is appropriate to restrict them by stating that a month or more must have passed during his absence, which indicates this.
ai.seo_question: Is a divorce valid if the husband pronounces it while absent and knows his wife is menstruating?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Istibsar* clarifies the fiqh of *Talaq al-Gha'ib* (divorce of the absent husband), specifically addressing the common juristic concern of whether the wife's menstrual state invalidates the divorce if the husband is unaware. While the Imam affirms the validity even if she was menstruating, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan provides a crucial scholarly qualification, limiting this general permissibility to cases where the absence exceeds a month, thereby distinguishing it from short-term absences where the husband might reasonably expect her to be in a state of purity.
